small_guidance:
- Add larger-tile autotune configs targeting the 2048x8192x8192 shape: try BLOCK_M=128/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=32 with num_warps=8 num_stages=4, and BLOCK_M=256/BLOCK_N=128/BLOCK_K=32 num_warps=8 num_stages=4; also a BLOCK_M=64/BLOCK_N=256/BLOCK_K=32 variant for better N coverage.
- Use tf32 in tl.dot (allow_tf32=True) since inputs are fp32 — this roughly doubles tensor-core throughput on Ada and is the single biggest lever for an 8K×8K×8K GEMM.
- Cast A/B tiles to fp16 (or use input_precision='tf32') just before tl.dot to engage tensor cores; keep accumulator in fp32. Also bump num_stages to 4 for the larger BLOCK_K=64 configs to better overlap K-loop loads.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a tensor-core GEMM that explicitly converts A and B tiles to fp16 (or bf16) in-kernel before tl.dot, with fp32 accumulator — the current fp32×fp32 dot only uses CUDA cores and leaves >5x perf on the table for an 8K cube GEMM on Ada.
- Consider a split-K or persistent-tile design: with M=2048, N=8192 there are only 16×64=1024 output tiles at 128×128, which under-occupies the SMs late in the kernel; a persistent kernel with stream-K style K-splitting would keep all 128 SMs busy and reduce tail effect.
- Pre-transpose weight once in __init__ (not lazily on first forward) and store as fp16 contiguous (K,N) so the hot path skips both the cache check and any dtype conversion; epilogue (bias, scale, hardtanh, GELU) stays fused on the fp32 accumulator before the fp32 store.
